Case Study — Project 03

Ultrasonic Walking Stick

Individual Project · Senior Category · Rotary Regional STEM Fair · Grade 12
🏆 3rd Place, Senior Category

Overview

Building on what I'd learned from the solar tracker project, I wanted to design something with a more immediate, practical use: an assistive device to help visually impaired users detect obstacles in their path before making physical contact with them.

Objectives

  • Build an obstacle-detecting device that gives visually impaired users advance warning of nearby objects
  • Achieve response times fast enough to be useful at a normal walking pace
  • Validate the design's reliability against a range of real-world obstacle types and placements

Process

01

Sensing

Used an ultrasonic sensor to continuously measure distance to the nearest object ahead of the user.

02

Processing & alerting

An Arduino read the sensor's distance measurements and processed them at near-instantaneous speed, triggering an alert before the user could make physical contact with an obstacle.

03

Build & assembly

Wired the ultrasonic sensor to the Arduino and a breadboard, then assembled the sensor, Arduino, and battery into a compact unit mounted directly on the user for hands-free, forward-facing detection.

04

Field testing

Tested the assembled device outdoors, including near steps and other everyday obstacles, at a normal walking pace — to confirm it gave usable, timely feedback rather than just working under controlled lab conditions.

Outcomes

✓
3rd Place, Senior Category, Rotary Regional STEM Fair
✓
Reliably identified multiple types of obstacles across repeated tests
✓
Delivered feedback fast enough to be usable at normal walking speed, not just in slow, controlled conditions

This project pushed me to design not just for a working prototype, but for a real user under real conditions — a mindset I carry into every project since.
